parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Mechanical power $P$ can be calculated using the formula $P = Fv$.

Use the concept of work and the definition of power to show how this formula is derived.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The engine of a lorry provides $130\text{ kW}$ of power to the lorry's wheels when it is travelling at a constant speed of $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a straight horizontal road.

Show that the resistive force opposing the forward motion of the lorry is $5200\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
The lorry in (b) travels up a straight section of road that is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1}}

Fig. 3.1 (not to scale)

The lorry has mass $m$ and the acceleration of free fall is $g$.
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of $m$, $g$ and $\theta$, for the component of the weight of the lorry that acts parallel to the surface of the road.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The total resistive force remains unchanged at $5200\text{ N}$ and the engine now provides greater power to maintain the speed of $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The total mass $m$ of the lorry is $36\,000\text{ kg}$. The angle $\theta$ is $1.4^{\circ}$.

Determine the power, in $\text{kW}$, now provided by the engine.
